deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is part of a German set of notes on ancient history, in the style of lecture notes (cf. Heeren-type courses on Greek colonisation). It continues section 'cc. Kolonien in Unter Italien' from the previous page and then begins 'dd. Kolonien auf Sicilien'.

Content, in order:
(1) Tarentum, a Spartan colony, founded 707, one of the richest cities. Croton was founded 710 and Sybaris 720. All of these cities grew so rich that luxury set in soon after their founding.
(2) Pythagoras lived in Croton and founded a school there. The notes say the famous lawgivers Charondas and Zaleukus came from it.
(3) Sybaris and Croton quarrelled, and Croton destroyed Sybaris in 510. Athens founded Thurium near the old site around 446; it flourished but could not rival Sybaris.
(4) Locri Epizephyrii had Zaleukus as lawgiver. Rhegium and Cumae are listed, with Cumae 'famous for the oracle of the Sibyl'.
(5) Sicily: the Greeks settled only the east and south coasts. The chief city was Syracuse, a Corinthian colony made up of four towns. It had quarries nearby and a natural harbour one German mile in circumference.
(6) Heading '1. Periode, von der Stiftung von Syracus bis auf Gelon, 735–484'. The constitution was aristocratic; the sentence continues on folio 68 ('...Periode stiftete die Stadt schon mehrere Kolonien').

There are no derivations, formulas or computations to reconstruct. The only numbers are dates BC. The hand and subject suggest a student's or copyist's transcript of a history lecture bound into the Gauss Nachlass, not Gauss's own mathematical work. This is my inference and cannot be confirmed from the page alone.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics.

Historical slip: the notes derive Zaleukus (and Charondas) from the Pythagorean school. Zaleucus of Locri (c. 660 BC) predates Pythagoras (fl. c. 530 BC); this was a common ancient/18th-century confusion.
The phrase 'Rhegium, et Cumae, war berühmt durch das Orakel der Sibylla' attaches the Sibyl to Rhegium as well. The oracle belongs only to Cumae.
Minor date inconsistency: Gelon's seizure of Syracuse is given as 484 in the period heading. Folio 68 dates the expulsion of the rich to 485, and Gelon is usually dated 485 BC.

transcription_corrections: Section heading: read 'dd. Kolonien auf Sicilien.' rather than 'b. d. [?]'. It follows aa (Asia Minor), bb (Black Sea) and cc (Lower Italy).
Line 2: 'so wie Croton das 710 und Sybaris die 720 angelegt wurde', with 'wie' in place of 'war' and 'das/die' as superscript corrections.
Line 4–5: likely 'ein Luxus einriß, von dem wir jetzt schwerlich einen Begriff machen können'. The illegible gap is probably 'einen Begriff'.
'zerfielen mit einander': 'mit' is an interlinear insertion; the reading is correct.
'Rhegium, et Cumae': the 'et' may be the 'u.'/'&' abbreviation for 'und'.
Last line: probably 'Die Verfassung von Syracus war aristokratisch. In dieser', continuing on folio 68 as '...Periode stiftete die Stadt schon mehrere Kolonien'. 'Anfangs' is unlikely.
Period dates read '735 — 484'; the second figure appears to be 484, consistent with the heading on folio 68 ('484 — 466').
